Adjusted summary incorporating the May 2017 Beige Book:
- The FOMC’s June 14, 2017 statement remains cautiously optimistic: moderate growth, continued labor-market strengthening, below-2% inflation, a 25 bp hike to 1–1.25%, and plans to start gradual balance-sheet normalization while policy stays accommodative.
- The May 2017 Beige Book broadly corroborates this: most districts reported modest-to-moderate expansion and tight labor markets, with wage pressures particularly for skilled workers. Energy-sector activity improved, supporting regional growth. Housing was generally firmer than commercial real estate, and tourism was a tailwind in some areas.
- Offsetting factors: auto sales/lending were softer and CRE saw caution, consistent with SLOOS signals of tighter auto and CRE credit. Banks’ firmer pricing and use of rate floors point to slightly less accommodative credit conditions.
- Net take: Beige Book evidence of tight labor markets and improving energy nudges the tone modestly more positive than the SLOOS-only view, but lingering inflation shortfall and credit pockets of tightening still temper the outlook.
